notes: Units: seconds from time zero; bus numbers start at 1. At equal timestamps, mandatory arrivals and completions precede listed manual actions, then one automatic decision batch, then door starts and departures. Cutoff includes arrivals at that timestamp, cancels later demand and ends new automatic decisions. The temporal control window is start inclusive, end exclusive; its automatic components restore normal service at end. Manual bounded instructions may finish or expire during drain. Cohort includes all present just before its boundary plus births through cutoff, retaining original whole-journey clocks. until_recovered uses forward gap at most 110% of ideal; a convoy leader owns the long wrap arc. Stopping precedes overhead and sequential door service; both overlap holds. Starting extends the following travel segment after service/holds. True bypasses incur neither stopping nor starting penalties. A boarding_limit permits the specified number of new boardings per visit; existing boarding finishes. See scenario-guide.html for bounds and definitions.
name: Recover with short announced skips
description: 12 stops, 4 buses, 40-second segments, fixed arrivals at 3 passengers per stop per minute, four-stop rides, and 5-second stopping and starting delays. Hold Bus 1 for 60 seconds at minute 20. From minute 25 through 60, check every 5 seconds. A bus at a stop with more than 3.3 stops ahead and less than 2.7 behind announces one lead-in location, then two pattern locations: skip one and serve one, capped at 900 seconds. The bounded pattern may be assigned again on a later visit. Accepted drop-offs override skips; at least one bus stays unrestricted. Actual bypasses occur in the default run and both spacing and passenger time improve relative to One delay → bunching. Compare with the long six-stop lead-in.

model.calibration_notes: Illustrative teaching model; not empirically calibrated.

recovery_policy.rule_explanation: Polling comparison: use one ordered snapshot, once per visit. Holding has leader protection, 30-second action limit, 90-second total budget and two-visit cooldown. Service restrictions preserve accepted drop-offs; no temporal coverage guarantee is claimed. Use passenger-cost for destination safeguards.
